model: TUCB / TUHB Series universal wall-mount controller (Modbus RTU)
equipment_type: Thermostat / heat pump and unitary controller
applies_to: Neptronic TUCB24C6X2 (temperature) and TUHB24C6X2 (temperature and humidity) universal wall-mount controllers with 6 binary and 2 analog outputs, guide TUXB-Modbus Guide-190515.
summary: The TUCB and TUHB are Neptronic wall-mount controllers with built-in sensors, six binary and two analog outputs, for fan coils, heat pumps (with reversing valve and emergency heat options) and other unitary equipment. Over Modbus RTU they expose temperatures, humidity (TUHB), CO2, ramp demands, output states, mode, fan and setpoint control and the configuration registers.

addressing.note: This older guide prints a "Register Index" with a 4 prefix starting at 40000. Its introduction places the device address at holding register index 0 and the baud rate at index 1, which the table shows as 40000 and 40001, so wire address = printed number - 40000 (not the usual 40001 rule).

source.title: TUCB & TUHB Series Universal Wall-Mount Controller Modbus Communication Module User Guide
source.pages: p. 1 (protocol, register index 0/1/2), pp. 2-16 (holding register table)

notes: Every register is a 16-bit holding register; there are no 32-bit values.
Temperatures, setpoints and bands follow the Modbus temperature-unit bit of system option 1 (°C or °F); sensor readings and offsets are x100, setpoints and bands x10.
Do not apply the 40001 rule: in this guide 40000 is register 0.
Left out: the four ASCII product-name registers and register 40042 (all bits reserved).

integration.summary: Read holding registers with function 03 at the printed register index minus 40000 (40011 = address 11). Set the temperature unit for Modbus first, then use the mode, fan and setpoint registers for control.
integration.enable: Modbus is the controller's native protocol; set the address (1-246) and, if needed, a fixed baud rate and parity from the device menu or registers 0-2.
quirks: The table prints a 4 prefix on a 0-based register index (40000 = address 0), not the 40001 Modicon convention.
Baud register holds baud/100 (384 = 38400); 0 means automatic baud detection.
setup: RS-485 two-wire, RTU. Supported baud rates 9600, 19200, 38400 and 57600; automatic baud detection is the default.
Parity/stop bits come from the communication-port register: 1 = none + 2 stop, 2 = even + 1 stop, 3 = odd + 1 stop.
gotchas: Changing the Modbus temperature-unit bit changes the meaning of every temperature register at once.
Some registers only apply to models with a humidity, CO2 or other optional sensor.

address_note: address = 0-based Modbus wire (PDU) address; documented = as printed in the source.
